result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers lead with a trimmed autoplay loop, split the motion into three labelled beats, and offer a 0.25x slow-motion version with the timings. B adds a timestamped filmstrip so people who won't press play can still follow the motion, and it explicitly says to write 'not yet tested' rather than imply results. A makes small unsupported claims, such as the beats overlapping to about 400ms in total, and its still-frame fallback is tucked into the Figma spec frame. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the clip first and split the motion into three labelled beats with 0.25x slow-motion versions. A does better on fallback: its timestamped filmstrip lets reviewers who skip the video still see the motion and check the timings, and it explicitly says to write "not yet tested" rather than imply results. B is strong on what to watch for and on asking pointed feedback questions, but it makes some unsupported claims: that the beats overlap to about 400ms total, that users "never wonder" whether the tap registered, and that Figma can't reproduce the arc. Its still fallback is also tucked inside the spec frame.
